Final Fantasy VII

Sephiroth

Defensive aerial fighter: Shadow Flare zoning and surgical punishes

Fastest BRV 15F (Transience)Fastest HP 43F (Octaslash, Heaven's Light)Dash 81 (Below Average)ATK 111DEF 1111-hit HP YesHP links Yes

Standing in the meta

Tier A 8th of 30 — 2017 tournament tier list from dissidia.wiki (half matchup values, half expert player votes).

Sephiroth is 8th on the 2017 ranking, in tier A. The overview confirms a consistently high competitive placement, carried by his reliability at every level of play.

Overview

Sephiroth is a defensive aerial fighter able to fight up close as well as at range. His main strategy rests on Shadow Flare zoning, with the aim of forcing mistakes: the dodge cancel lets him chain Shadow Flares quickly, which hampers the opponent's movement, pushes them to approach and opens the way for the rest of his arsenal.

Sephiroth is versatile: he synergises well with the game's mechanics and thrives when the opponent has to come to him. Shadow Flare pressures melee fighters and spellcasters alike, while filling the assist gauge at a steady rate. Sudden Cruelty complements the projectiles up close with its disjointed hitbox and its strong damage and EX potential. His combos are solid thanks to his assist synergy (Kuja and Aerith), and his defensive options after an aerial dodge are formidable: Heaven's Light and Hell's Gate are vertical, evasive HP attacks, Scintilla guards instantly from frame 1 (staggering dashes and low priority melee attacks), and Heaven's Light even guarantees HP damage after an escape with LV2 Assist Change.

He is not without weaknesses: Bravery Boost on Dodge builds discourage overusing Shadow Flare, many of his attacks are telegraphed (HP attacks, Oblivion) or linear (Godspeed, Sudden Cruelty), his fast-startup bravery attacks are paid for with longer than average recovery, and his mobility is below average. Even after a dodge, picking the right defensive option remains a gamble, and he has to keep an eye on vertical tracking, Precision Evasion and the opponent's command blocks so as not to overexpose himself.

Competitively, Sephiroth is consistently ranked high in the hierarchy. His low execution floor and reliable aerial combat make him an excellent character for beginners and seasoned players alike, and he is particularly hard to beat at low and intermediate levels. His very action-oriented style helps him more than it hurts, provided the player does not become a slave to their own habits.

Strengths

  • Zoning: Shadow Flare puts the opponent under pressure and dictates the pace of the match.
  • Aerial combat: Sephiroth fights comfortably without depending on the ground.
  • High damage: a big attack stat, large base damage and HP Wall Rushes — a single assist combo can shred the opponent's bravery.
  • Reliable EX and assist gauge generation.
  • Builds with plenty of room for optimisation and fine-tuning.
  • Flexible post-dodge defence: three aerial HP attacks providing evasion or an instant guard.
  • An EX Mode that amplifies his damage and unlocks Heartless Angel (the opponent's bravery reduced to 1); a simple, reliable character at every level.

Weaknesses

  • Anti-zoning: Bravery Boost on Dodge and long-range counters (Firion's Shield Bash, Exdeath's block followups) limit how effective his zoning is.
  • Linearity: many attacks that are telegraphed or have average to poor tracking.
  • No fast aerial poke: no move combines a fast startup with an early dodge cancel — the sole exception, Transience, only exists on the ground.
  • Below-average mobility overall, which pushes him to act rather than to move without committing.

Moves

Bravery attacks

Ground

Reaper 21FMelee Low

A three-part ground combo, Sephiroth's high-damage ground punish (21F). Delaying each Circle press until a flurry has finished maximises the number of hits, and therefore the damage; stopped at the second part, Reaper starts assist combos, and walls reduce the knockback of the final hit so that it converts too. It needs a dodge cancel to be made safe on whiff, and Sephiroth's heavily aerial game limits his chances to use it.

Fervent Blow 27FMelee Low, Ranged Low

A linear stream of ground projectiles, to be used sparingly as a mid-range whiff punish: its active time covers attacks with gaps such as Prishe's Raging Fists, and it starts assist combos on the projectile or after a Wall Rush. Long recovery, Ranged Low priority, no tracking: vulnerable to lateral movement, Ground Dash and Free Air Dash. The close-range sword strike, which carries melee priority, tends to cross up against a block from very close range, a potential mixup against guard — but Godspeed, its aerial equivalent, sees more use.

Aerial

Sudden Cruelty 17FMelee Low

A two-part aerial combo and Sephiroth's major aerial punish (17F, unreactable): his reference offensive poke up close, with a disjointed hitbox that reaches its maximum range quickly. Excellent for starting and padding assist combos, it reliably converts a close Shadow Flare hit and can even pierce high-priority projectiles when well positioned. Weakness: almost no movement towards the opponent — it struggles to catch evasive movement, Ground Dash first among them.

Godspeed 23FMelee Low, Ranged Low

The aerial version of the linear projectile stream: a mid-range whiff punish thanks to its startup and its active frames, able to contest attacks with gaps (Tifa's feints) from a distance, with a Wall Rush on the ground to start an assist combo. No horizontal or vertical tracking: the projectiles fly straight, which exposes him to assist punishes. It competes with Oblivion for the third bravery slot: Godspeed has more lateral reach and damage, Oblivion better vertical coverage; on a hit at range against a grounded opponent, a dodge cancel into Sudden Cruelty can combo on the landing lag.

Oblivion 27FMelee Low

Sephiroth passes through the opponent then delivers a series of hits with a downward Wall Rush, good for assist combos on the ground. It is his melee bravery attack with the longest vertical reach (he closes in during the startup): perfect for punishing careless opponents above or below him and badly placed assists, but reactable otherwise. After a Shadow Flare hit, Oblivion follows up more easily than his other bravery attacks; with lock-on off and assigned to Circle, it doubles as movement in any direction to fill the assist gauge more safely.

Shadow Flare (midair) 45FRanged Low

The projectile that defines Sephiroth: four long-range orbs that surround the opponent before converging. Generous range, a fast cancel into other actions, combo starters: it is the heart of his zoning, it forces the opponent to approach, harasses setup characters such as Kefka and Ultimecia and fills the assist gauge quickly. Its weaknesses are real: Ranged Low (a dash goes straight through it), tracking that stops the moment it activates, no protection for Sephiroth's own body, telegraphed (vulnerable to Firion's Shield Bash, Exdeath's Omni Block) and counterproductive against Bravery Boost on Dodge builds.

Ground

Black Materia 63FRanged High

A projectile chargeable in three levels: only level 3, which falls vertically onto the opponent, deals bravery damage and Wall Rush, and Sephiroth can move while it drops. Little used competitively: very slow startup, complete immobility, no protection — the angle of the meteors leaves Sephiroth open to dashes and interruptions from close and far alike. Aerial

Hell's Gate 55FMelee High

A flexible dive (55F) to threaten the ground, to defend after an aerial dodge or to finish an assist combo. Square held: a multi-hit dive that drags the opponent downwards, with a ground burst carrying an HP hitbox on landing; released: a transition into a single-hit HP attack. The rise during the startup provides a measure of evasion and Sephiroth steers manually throughout the attack; every version converts into an assist combo, extendable with Aerith. Held, it even becomes an infinite combo in Phantom Train by pushing the opponent towards a window.

Identical to the ground version, but its existence in the air makes it a pillar of Sephiroth's defence: a frame 1 command block, it stops many dodge punish attempts dead, Free Air Dash first among them. Heaven's Light 43FMelee High

A single-hit evasive HP attack (43F) with the right knockback for ceiling Wall Rushes: Sephiroth places himself under the opponent then shoots upwards. Excellent as a punish, as an assist combo finisher, as protection after an aerial dodge and as a whiff callout; the initial dive dodges many attacks without being invincibility. Reliable after an LV2 Assist Change stagger to secure HP damage, hard to punish thanks to the long distance it covers and its short recovery for an HP attack — an essential move, and a valuable one for gauge depletion through Wall Rush.

EX Mode: Reunion! & EX Burst

The “Reunion!” EX Mode grants Regen, Critical Boost, Glide (free flight by holding Cross in the air) and Heartless Angel. Sephiroth's bravery damage being good already, he naturally benefits from critical hits; with the assist and EX gauges full, a single assist combo followed by an EX Mode activation creates enormous momentum.

Heartless Angel (R + Square): Sephiroth charges an unblockable attack that reduces the opponent's bravery to 1 (he cannot gain bravery while charging). A charge time of 5 seconds (297 frames), with a cooldown of about 0.6 seconds if the button is released early. Assists can follow up behind it, which generally guarantees a bravery break; assists that hold the opponent for a long time (Jecht, Kuja) work around the long charge. Even without the time to charge it fully, starting it pushes the opponent to approach. If the opponent's bravery is already at 1, it is not reduced any further.

EX Burst : The Super Nova EX Burst fills by mashing Circle: simple execution and one of the most powerful bursts in the game (100 base damage in total).

Special moves

Special commands that never appear in the equip lists: they cost no CP and trigger from a dedicated input.

Heartless Angel Special moveR + Square held — EX Mode (One-Winged Angel) only

A special attack absent from the equipment lists, available only in EX Mode: after a long charge time that leaves Sephiroth vulnerable, it instantly reduces the opponent's bravery to 1 if it goes through. It fails if Sephiroth is in a Break state when the charge finishes. It ignores protective summons such as Demon Wall, and against a bravery freeze (Alexander) it forces a freeze at 1. EX Mode also brings Glide: holding X lets him glide.

Gameplan & advanced tech

Sephiroth's neutral starts with Shadow Flare: harass at range, fill the assist gauge and convert into a combo when possible — without expecting direct damage from it. The threat of the projectile forces the opponent to approach, and that is where the rest of the arsenal takes over: Sudden Cruelty punishes aerial dodges and careless attacks up close, Godspeed and Fervent Blow whiff punish at mid range, Oblivion covers the vertical.

His solo combos revolve around Shadow Flare: a dodge cancel into Sudden Cruelty (43~52 base damage, 87 EX), a cancel into Oblivion for less risk, or a direct cancel into Heaven's Light — the most consistent one, which works even above the opponent thanks to the move's automatic movement. In EX Revenge, the reference routine is five Shadow Flares chained then Heaven's Light, and it works anywhere.

With an assist (Kuja), the classic starters are the first part of Sudden Cruelty, Reaper stopped at two hits, Oblivion's ground Wall Rush or an Octaslash Wall Rush; Heaven's Light serves as a reliable, low-execution finisher, Sudden Cruelty or Hell's Gate as EX-oriented finishers, Octaslash as a damage finisher that gives base bravery the time to recover.

Defensively, Sephiroth's strength is his post-dodge flexibility: Scintilla (frame 1) against dashes and low-priority bravery attacks, Heaven's Light and Hell's Gate as vertical evasive exits — not forgetting that Heaven's Light guarantees HP damage after an LV2 Assist Change stagger. Every option has a counter, so vary them: that is the price of his mediocre mobility and his long recoveries.

Beware the character's pitfalls: Bravery Boost on Dodge builds punish overusing Shadow Flare, and Sephiroth's very active style can let the player fall back into their own habits. Control the pace, and only engage once the zoning has prepared the ground.

Character-specific tech

Hell's Gate Infinite (Phantom Train)

A held Hell's Gate becomes an infinite combo in Phantom Train: Sephiroth steers towards one of the carriage windows while hitting the opponent during the multi-hit dive.

Shadow Flare cross-cancel

The ground Shadow Flare can be cancelled into an aerial Shadow Flare, whereas the aerial version cannot be cancelled into itself. A minor detail, but a useful one for Pre-Jump builds that want to leave the ground without deactivating the booster.

Blodge after Shadow Flare

During Shadow Flare's recovery, Sephiroth can blodge to stagger an opponent dashing at him, then convert: Heaven's Light if the dodge has not carried him too far away (guaranteed HP damage and depletion), bravery attacks or an assist otherwise. Recommended at intermediate and advanced levels rather than to beginners.

Oblivion lock-off movement

With lock-on off and Oblivion assigned to Circle, Sephiroth can use it to move in any direction he is facing — a way to fill the assist gauge more safely.

Godspeed landing lag combo

If Godspeed's projectiles hit a grounded opponent at range, a dodge cancel into Sudden Cruelty can combo on the landing lag. The dodge cancel timing is noticeably later on hit, which takes practice.

Hell's Gate input hold

To make sure a Hell's Gate does not stop early when a BRV assist is called: hold Square, then also hold Circle and press L. The input is awkward (thumb + left index finger) but it makes the setup reliable, notably on a clash with a charged One Inch Punch.

Documented solo combo routes

Many routes around Shadow Flare, very few outside it, all of them dealing very high damage: Shadow Flare > dodge cancel > anything; level 3 Black Materia > Reaper or Octaslash; point-blank Godspeed > landing lag > Godspeed > landing lag > Sudden Cruelty.

Matchups

Only one matchup is documented in detail: Prishe (even). The two characters fight over position and EX gauge; Sephiroth wants to harass with Shadow Flare before closing in, Prishe wants to get into contact. The big exchanges happen up close, where every action has a counter — none of Sephiroth's tools is risk-free, so he has to vary them. The matchup calls for a good understanding of positioning, gauge management and timings, but Sephiroth has the tools to come out of it well (recommended build: EX or damage).

In neutral: fill the assist gauge with Shadow Flare then convert into assist combos (finished with Sudden Cruelty for EX or Heaven's Light for HP). Godspeed is exceptional here, whereas it sees little use elsewhere: its burst interrupts a charged One Inch Punch, during the charge or on release, provided he is at the same height as Prishe. Dodging above her exploits the mediocre vertical tracking of her moves. Sudden Cruelty catches the aerial dodges that leave her close, punishes anticipated HP attacks and stops her rushes — but be careful not to whiff punish a charged OIP with it, on pain of a stagger.

On defence: Scintilla establishes that Prishe cannot dash in and hit for free (Free Air Dash, Raging Fists, uncharged OIP), ideally after a dodge — but it protects against neither a charged OIP nor Banishga. Against Banishga: a neutral dodge at the moment of impact then a whiff punish (Sudden Cruelty, Reaper or assist), or vertical dodges. Assist Changes are central: LV1 Change > Heaven's Light against Auroral Uppercut, LV1 Change as soon as Banishga starts > Free Air Dash > Sudden Cruelty, LV2 Change > Heaven's Light against OIP, Dragon Kick or Auroral Uppercut. Under Assist Lock, slow the pace down and keep moving (Quickmoves, Multi Air Slide, jumps).

On offence: Sephiroth rarely attacks — HP attacks work against a block as a mixup after a dash (condition with bravery attacks first), Sudden Cruelty catches the startup of Free Air Dash, Hell's Gate on landing beats ground dodges, and the “checkmate” EX Revenge allows constant Free Air Dashes with an EX Revenge reaction on hit. Watch out for block > Nullifying Dropkick on the ground. On builds: EX with Cleaver/White Gem and Aerith (more EX and ATK but dependent on Chase setups), or EX with Heaven's Cloud and other assists (easier EX outside Chase with Tenacious Attacker, whiff punishes possible, less damage).

Match videos: Replay Theater — Sephiroth matches.

Builds

Sephiroth works with a great many builds, bravery damage and EX being his bread and butter; his builds leave plenty of room for optimisation. The documented build is a “Seal of Lufenia” hybrid with the Equip Glitch (the total CP cost assumes the glitch has been performed): One-Winged Angel as the weapon, Lufenian pieces (Dirk, Hairpin, Vest), Kuja assist, Rubicante summon and a battery of booster accessories (Hyper Ring, Muscle Belt, Sniper Eye, Battle Hammer, the Summon Unused / Pre-EX Mode / Aerial / Opponent Summon Unused conditions, Tenacious Attacker, Glutton) for a maximum multiplier of x3.5 — 1175 BRV, 180 ATK, 182 DEF. The Best Dresser extra ability is the one to equip.

The matchups page sheds complementary light on the EX trade-offs: an EX build with Cleaver, White Gem and the Aerith assist maximises EX gain and ATK but depends on Aerith's Chase setups; an EX build with Heaven's Cloud and other assists makes EX easier on Sudden Cruelty without Chase (Tenacious Attacker recommended) and allows HP attacks to be whiff punished with an assist, at the cost of lower bravery damage.

Assist synergies

Sephiroth as an assist

Sephiroth sits in the High tier of the assist tier list. His assist attacks: Reaper (ground BRV, 21F, 45 base damage, Chase), Sudden Cruelty (air BRV, 17F, 40 damage, Chase), Octaslash (ground HP, 43F, Wall Rush) and Hell's Gate (air HP, 55F, Chase). On Cloud's page he is described as a “budget” Kuja with a better whiff punish; the Hell's Gate assist helps out in scrambles, despite a cost that is sometimes hard to justify.

Recommended assists

  • Kuja — Cited alongside Aerith as a pillar of the assist synergy that makes Sephiroth's combos complete; he is the assist of the documented build and of every detailed combo route (Sudden Cruelty, Reaper, Oblivion, Octaslash, Heaven's Light as starters).
  • Aerith — The second pillar of the assist synergy according to the overview; she extends Hell's Gate conversions in particular and feeds the Chase-based EX build described in the Prishe matchup.
  • Tidus / Yuna — Mentioned in the Prishe matchup as more consistent conversions than Kuja after Godspeed's projectiles (Tidus ground BRV > Shadow Flare > Heaven's Light; Yuna ground BRV with a wall), at the cost of less destructive routes — acceptable given Prishe's low base defence.

Known limits

  • No unique mechanic is documented for Sephiroth (the section is absent from the wiki).
  • Only one matchup is detailed (Prishe); the rest of the cast is not covered.
  • The assist synergy section amounts to a single sentence (“works with most tournament-viable assists”): the recommendations above are reconstructed from the overview and the Prishe matchup.
  • The second build is entirely empty and the attack selections of the builds are not filled in.
  • The assist gauge gain values (assistGain) are empty for every move, and Heaven's Light's damage is not quantified (“-”).
  • The wiki's only reference is a URL with no title, author or date.
